title: Money-Mouth Face Emoji 🤑 Meaning: Payday or Greed?
description: The money-mouth face emoji 🤑 means money is on someone's mind: payday, a big sale, a side hustle, or plain greed. See what it implies and why scammers love it.
summary: 🤑 has dollar signs for eyes and a banknote for a tongue. It means the sender is excited about money: getting paid, landing a deal, finding a bargain or picturing a profit. It can celebrate success or poke fun at greed, depending on who it is aimed at.
meaning: The simplest use is celebration. Payday hits, a commission clears, a freelance invoice finally gets paid, and 🤑 goes into the group chat. It says “I have money and I am thrilled about it.” The cartoonish design keeps it from sounding like a real boast, which is why people who would never post their salary will happily post this face.

It is equally common before the money exists. Someone listing old sneakers online, pitching a business idea or placing a fantasy football bet uses 🤑 for the cash they imagine is coming. The emoji borrows from old cartoons where a character's eyes turn into dollar signs when they spot an opportunity. That reference is the whole point: the sender is admitting, with a grin, that money is driving them.

Turned on someone else, it becomes a comment on greed. Replying 🤑 to news that a company raised prices again, or that a celebrity launched yet another product line, means “they're just in it for the money.” Friends use it more gently to tease the one in the group who always splits the bill to the cent or who just got a raise.

There is one setting where it should raise your guard. Get-rich-quick posts, crypto pumps, betting tipsters and “DM me to learn how I made $5k this week” comments are packed with 🤑. The emoji is not proof of a scam, but a stranger promising easy money with a row of these faces is a pattern worth recognizing.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Friends send it on payday, after selling something, or when a refund lands. It also answers good financial news from someone else, as in “you got the bonus? 🤑.” Among close friends it can be a nudge that the lucky one is buying the next round, said as a joke with a little hope behind it.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Side-hustle, reselling and investing content uses 🤑 in captions and thumbnails to promise earnings. Shoppers use it for hauls and big discounts. In comment sections it is often sarcastic, dropped under sponsored posts or pricey product launches to suggest the creator has sold out.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Sales teams use it in chat when a deal closes, and it is common around bonus season among peers. It is risky in front of clients or in company-wide channels, where cheering about money can look tacky. It should never appear in a message about someone else's pay.

contexts.label: In sports
contexts.body: Fans post it when a player signs a huge contract or when a bet pays out. Sports betting accounts use it heavily to advertise winning picks. Under transfer and free-agency news it often carries a hint of criticism, implying the athlete chose the paycheck over loyalty or a better team.

examples.meaning: Payday has arrived and the sender is celebrating.

examples.text: Sold my old camera for more than I paid for it 🤑
examples.meaning: Pleased about making an unexpected profit.
Excited about a sale and the money saved, not earned.

examples.text: Another subscription price hike. Of course 🤑
examples.meaning: Sarcastic; accusing a company of being greedy.

examples.text: Look at you with the promotion 🤑 drinks on you Friday?
examples.meaning: Congratulating a friend and jokingly volunteering them to pay.

examples.text: If this parlay hits I'm retiring 🤑
examples.meaning: Daydreaming about a big gambling win that probably will not happen.

combos.meaning: A lot of money was made or is expected; a straightforward celebration of profit.
Money is coming in and going straight back out, often on a shopping spree.
An investment, stock or sales number is climbing and the sender is delighted.
A deal has been closed that pays well for both sides.

confusedWith.difference: 💰 is the money itself: a prize, a salary, a price tag. 🤑 is a person's reaction to money. Use 💰 to label an amount and 🤑 to show how badly someone wants it or how happy they are to have it.
💸 shows cash flying away and usually means spending, losing or sending money. 🤑 is about gaining or craving it. “Rent due 💸” and “bonus day 🤑” point in opposite directions.
🤩 has stars for eyes and expresses awe or excitement about anything. 🤑 replaces the stars with dollar signs, narrowing the excitement to money specifically.

avoid: Do not send it to someone who has just told you they are struggling financially.
Avoid it when discussing inheritance, insurance payouts or settlements, where money is tied to loss.
Keep it out of client-facing messages about pricing, since it makes you look eager to take their money.
design: A yellow face with dollar signs in place of eyes and a tongue hanging out that is drawn as a green banknote or stamped with a dollar sign. Most vendors show a wide grin; the shade of green and the details on the tongue vary. The symbol is a dollar sign on every major platform, regardless of the user's own currency.

faqs.a: No. It means they are excited about money at this moment, which could be a twenty-dollar refund. People use it far more for small wins, sales and daydreams than for real wealth.

It can be. Used about yourself it is cheerful. Aimed at a company, influencer or athlete, it often implies they are greedy or have sold out. Check whether the sender is celebrating their own gain or commenting on someone else's motives.

Because it instantly signals profit. Posts promising fast returns from crypto, betting tips or “simple” online jobs use 🤑 to grab attention. The emoji is not a warning sign by itself, but unsolicited promises of easy money decorated with it deserve suspicion.

faqs.q: What does 🤑 mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: Nothing romantic. Whoever sends it is talking about money: a paycheck, a deal, or a joke about you paying. If it follows a mention of your new job or purchase, it is light teasing about your finances.
The money-mouth face was approved in 2015 alongside 🤔, 🤗, 🙄 and 🤐, and it reached iPhone and Android keyboards in the months that followed.
